title: Frontend senior scenario component ownership conflict
topic: Frontend senior scenario component ownership conflict
question: How would you resolve this, both the immediate conflict and the underlying process gap?
idealAnswer:
Separate the immediate tactical problem (Team B is now shipping a duplicated, drifting fork) from the underlying process problem (there's no clear, timely path for teams to request changes to shared components)

Get both teams' actual constraints on the table, Team A's consistency concern and Team B's deadline, rather than treating it as a pure yes/no request, there's often a design that satisfies both, like a constrained variant within the existing system

Advocate for stopping the fork quickly, forked components are a long-term consistency and maintenance liability, the cost compounds the longer it exists

Propose or reinforce a concrete contribution process for the shared library, e.g. an RFC-lite process with a committed SLA for review, so future requests don't escalate to forking out of frustration

Consider whether the shared component's ownership model itself needs to change, e.g. a rotating review committee across teams instead of one team acting as a bottleneck gatekeeper, if this kind of conflict is recurring rather than one-off

Recognize this as fundamentally a communication and process issue as much as a technical one, and address it as such rather than purely dictating a technical resolution
